title: Indian Parliament & executive
examples: What is the main difference between the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha?
Who is the head of the government in India?
What powers does the President of India hold?

explain.say: The President of India is the constitutional head of the country.
The Prime Minister is the actual head of the government.
The Lok Sabha is the lower house of the Indian Parliament.
The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Indian Parliament.
The Parliament consists of the President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha.
When the government wants to pass a major law, both houses must agree.

draw.text: Law needs agreement from both houses.

faq.q: Does the President make laws by themselves?
faq.a: No, the President gives assent to laws passed by Parliament. The President acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
asks: Who signs the bill into law?
What is the President's role in lawmaking?

faq.q: Who is the most powerful person in the government?
faq.a: The Prime Minister is the head of the government and leads the cabinet. The Prime Minister holds the real executive power.
asks: Who runs the day-to-day work of the government?
Is the PM more powerful than the President?

faq.q: Which house is more powerful, the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha?
faq.a: The Lok Sabha is generally considered more powerful because its members are directly elected by the people. The Lok Sabha can pass no-confidence motions.
asks: Which house represents the people more directly?
Can the Lok Sabha dismiss the government?

faq.q: How are the members of the Rajya Sabha chosen?
faq.a: Members of the Rajya Sabha are chosen by the elected legislatures of the states. They do not vote directly for these members.
asks: Do people vote for Rajya Sabha members?
What body elects Rajya Sabha members?

faq.q: What is the main difference between the two houses?
faq.a: The Lok Sabha represents the will of the people directly, while the Rajya Sabha represents the interests of the states. This is their main difference.
asks: What is the main function difference?

facts: The President acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.
The Prime Minister is the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha.
Lok Sabha members are chosen through direct elections by the citizens.
Rajya Sabha members are chosen by the elected members of the state legislatures.

quiz.say: The person who signs a bill into an Act is the:
quiz.why: The President's assent is required for a bill to become law.

wrong.0: The Speaker oversees the proceedings but does not give final assent.
wrong.1: The Chairman presides over the Rajya Sabha but does not give final assent.
wrong.3: The Prime Minister leads the government but does not give final assent to laws.

quiz.say: If a law needs to be passed, which house represents the direct will of the people?
quiz.why: The Lok Sabha members are directly elected by the voters of India.

wrong.0: The Rajya Sabha is indirectly elected by state bodies, not directly by the public.
wrong.1: The President is the constitutional head, not a legislative body.
wrong.2: The Prime Minister is the head of the executive, not a legislative house.

quiz.say: Which body is responsible for representing the interests of the states in Parliament?
quiz.why: The Rajya Sabha is specifically designed to represent the interests of the various states.

wrong.0: The Prime Minister leads the central government, not the state representation.
wrong.2: The Lok Sabha focuses primarily on the will of the entire nation's population.
wrong.3: The President acts as a unifying figure, not a representative of specific states.
